newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-CHINA RETAIN WOMEN'S TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-CHINA RETAIN WOMEN'S TITLE.

text.p: China won the women's team title for the 11th time at the world table tennis championships on Tuesday, whitewashing North Korea 3-0 in their 14th consecutive final.
With three players ranked among the top five in the world, the Chinese proved impreganable, emerging undefeated from their eight matches.

Deng Yaping, the 24-year-old world champion and Atlanta Olympic gold medallist, maintained her 100 percent record by beating 17-year-old Kim Hyon Hui 21-15 21-14. The world number one, sensing the nervousness of her young opponent, did not hit with her usual power and even let up in the second game when she led 11-3.

World No.4 Yang Ying had given the champions a winning start against the left-handed Wi Bok Sun. But the 20-year-old was pressed to the wire in the opening set when she failed to read her opponent's heavy spin serves and was taken to deuce after leading 20-17.
However, the North Korean could not maintain the tempo and Yang went on to complete a 22-20 21-16 victory.
By the time Deng had made her entrance and then exited triumphantly, any challenge to the Chinese had disappeared as world No.5 Li Ju faced Korean Tu Jong Sil, ranked 63 places below her.

It was a mountain too high for Tu. Li simply swept through 21-8 21-14 to keep the Chinese on track to repeat their 1995 clean sweep of all seven titles with the men defending their crown in Wednesday's final.

It was the fourth time North Korea had lost the women's team final against China following defeat in 1979, 1985 and 1993. The North and South fielded a united women's team in 1991 and took the title away from China.
Chinese women's team coach Lu Yuansheng was full of praise for his team, particularly singling out Yang, who was making her world championship team debut..

"That first set was very important. She is a young player and she got a little bit nervous. It was very close, but she won on deuce and and this stimulated the other players. With Deng Yaping following, you couldn't have had a better player. She has all that experience and our team has the right mix of older players and young players."

Deng said this was her fifth championship appearance, but there was a very diffent feeling in the Chinese team. "I am delighted to win this title again with these young players. It feels different, with fewer older players and more new young players."
Deng, who claimed the doubles as well as the singles titles at the last world championships and the Atlanta Olympics, said her drive for success was still strong.
